questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Fenestrated capillaries are absent in__________
questions.explanation:
Fenestrated capillaries are absent in the lungs.

Fenestrated capillaries contain gaps between endothelial cells and occur where passage of larger molecules is required, including renal glomeruli, endocrine glands, intestinal mucosa and pancreas.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following layers of a large blood vessel wall does the vasa vasorum supply blood to?

options.text: Tunica adventitia and outer part of Tunica media
Tunica adventitia, Tunica media and outer part of Tunica intima

questions.correctAnswerText: Tunica adventitia and outer part of Tunica media
questions.explanation:
Vasa vasorum is a network of small vessels supplying the tunica adventitia and outer tunica media of large vessels.

Small arteries are nourished by diffusion from luminal blood; in larger arteries diffusion becomes inadequate, so vasa vasorum supply the adventitia and outer media while the intima and inner media are nourished from the lumen.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Collateral circulation refers to circulation through _______
questions.explanation:
Circulation through anastomoses is called collateral circulation.

Anastomoses may be arterial, venous or arteriovenous. Examples include palmar/plantar arches and Circle of Willis for arterial anastomoses, dorsal venous arches for venous anastomoses, and AV shunts in skin, lips, ears, nasal/intestinal mucosa and erectile tissue.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding arteries?

options.text: Arteries have valves to allow unidirectional flow

questions.explanation:
Umbilical arteries carry deoxygenated blood from the heart to the placenta during fetal life.

Arteries generally carry oxygenated blood away from the heart; pulmonary and umbilical arteries are exceptions carrying deoxygenated blood.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A middle-aged patient with recently detected hypertension is started on calcium channel blockers to reduce blood pressure by decreasing the peripheral vascular resistance. Which of the following vessels primarily contribute to the peripheral resistance to blood flow?
questions.explanation:
Muscular arterioles contribute the major part of peripheral resistance to blood flow.

Arterioles are the smallest muscular arteries and have relatively thick tunica media. They produce the largest pressure drop before capillary beds, are densely sympathetically innervated, and are regulated mainly by local vasoactive/metabolic factors with central mechanisms also contributing.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following are end arteries?
questions.explanation:
All the other arteries in the source's missing numbered list except the posterior cerebral artery are described as end arteries.

End arteries are terminal arteries whose branches do not anastomose adequately with neighboring branches. True/anatomic end arteries have no anastomoses (e.g. central retinal and internal auditory arteries); functional end arteries have inadequate anastomoses (e.g. segmental renal arteries).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following veins have valves?
questions.explanation:
Testicular veins have valves.

Venous valves maintain unidirectional blood flow. The source lists valve absence in veins less than 2 mm, venae cavae, and hepatic, renal, uterine, ovarian, cerebral, spinal, pulmonary and umbilical veins; it also notes the fetal Eustachian valve of the IVC.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: In which of the following structures are the sinusoids not present?
questions.explanation:
Sinusoids are absent in parotid glands.

Sinusoids are large irregular vascular spaces with true discontinuities in their walls, allowing close contact between blood and organ parenchyma. The source lists liver, spleen, bone marrow, suprarenal glands, adenohypophysis, parathyroid glands and carotid body as sites containing sinusoids.

questions.question: Compared to their corresponding arteries, the veins do not have
questions.explanation: Compared with corresponding arteries, veins have much less muscular and elastic tissue, consistent with lower venous pressure.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following vessels belong to the circulatory system referred to as the drainage system of coarse type?
questions.explanation:
The thoracic duct and right lymphatic duct are lymphatic-system vessels described as the drainage system of coarse type.

The lymphatic system removes larger particles such as proteins and particulate matter from tissue fluid; the venous system is described as the drainage system of fine type.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following lymphoid tissue has both afferent and efferent lymphatics?
questions.explanation:
Lymph nodes have both afferent and efferent lymphatics. Afferent lymphatics enter at multiple points on the periphery and efferent lymphatics leave at the hilum.

The source notes that tonsils, thymus and spleen have no afferent lymphatics.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: An 86-year-old woman presented with sepsis and a massive right pleural effusion. She developed a chylous effusion 2 days after a chest tube insertion. An injury to the thoracic duct is suspected. Which of the following parts is not drained by it?
questions.explanation:
The right upper limb drains into the right lymphatic duct rather than the thoracic duct.

The thoracic duct drains both lower limbs, left upper limb, abdomen, left half of thorax and left side of head/neck. The right lymphatic duct drains the right upper limb, right half of thorax and right side of head/neck.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding lymph capillaries is false?
questions.explanation:
Lymph capillaries are wider than blood capillaries, so the statement that they are narrower is false.

They begin blindly in tissue spaces, form networks, have thin permeable endothelial walls and relatively lower pressure than blood capillaries.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: How many spinal nerves are present in the cervical region?
questions.explanation:
There are 8 pairs of cervical spinal nerves.

The cerebrospinal nervous system includes 12 pairs of cranial nerves and 31 pairs of spinal nerves: 8 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral and 1 coccygeal.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Bipolar neurons are present in all of the following except ______
questions.explanation:
Bipolar neurons are not seen in spinal ganglia; spinal ganglia contain pseudounipolar neurons.

Examples listed: unipolar neurons in mesencephalic nucleus, pseudounipolar neurons in sensory/spinal ganglia, bipolar neurons in spiral and vestibular ganglia and retina, and multipolar neurons in cerebrum and cerebellum.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: While trying to grab a cup of coffee, you suddenly withdrew your hands from the cup as it was too hot. The reflex arc responsible for this quick action is made up of all the parts except:
questions.explanation:
A reflex arc contains an effector, usually a muscle, not an affector.

A monosynaptic reflex arc consists of receptor, sensory/afferent neuron, motor/efferent neuron and effector.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following neuroglial cells is not derived from neuroectoderm?
questions.explanation:
Microglial cells are not neuroectodermal; they are mesoderm-derived, possibly from circulating monocytes entering the CNS during fetal/early postnatal life.

Macroglia of neuroectodermal origin include astrocytes, oligodendrocytes and glioblasts.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following is not a component of the blood-brain barrier?

options.text: End feet of astrocytes covering the capillary walls

questions.explanation:
Fenestrated capillary endothelium is not part of the blood-brain barrier.

The blood-brain barrier consists of capillary endothelium with tight junctions and no fenestrations, endothelial basement membrane, and astrocyte end-feet covering capillary walls. It permits selective passage of blood constituents into nervous tissue.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The nerve plexuses are formed only by ______
questions.explanation:
Nerve plexuses are formed only by ventral rami.

The spinal nerve exits the intervertebral foramen and divides into ventral and dorsal rami. Cervical, brachial, lumbar, sacral and coccygeal plexuses are formed from ventral rami, not dorsal rami.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A patient was rushed to the hospital with an alleged history of overdose with a sympathomimetic drug. Which of the following signs would you not expect to see due to the sympathetic stimulation of the drug?
questions.explanation:
Dry skin is not expected with sympathetic stimulation.

The sympathetic nervous system arises from the lateral horn of T1-L2 spinal segments (thoracolumbar outflow). Sympathetic effects listed include sweating (sudomotor), arrector-pili contraction (pilomotor), raised blood pressure (vasomotor), dilated pupils, dry mouth and tachycardia.

Examples of sympathomimetic drugs listed are phenylephrine, albuterol, cocaine and amphetamines.
